text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- A special coalition council should solve the problems within the coalition concerning the sale of the government's 70-percent voting stake in Creditanstalt, Social Democrat Chancellor Franz Vranitzky said. Conservative Vice-Chancellor Wolfgang Schuessel has said his party would attend such a meeting.
- Both Social Democrats and Conservatives speak of a break in trust by the other party in the ongoing coalition crisis.

- State secretary Karl Schloegl expects the European Commission to accept the higher fees for trucks on Austria's motorways, while his party colleague transport minister Rudolf Scholten does not see the problem solved.
- Vranitzky sees no need to slow down decisions about the sale of Creditanstalt, even though a special parliamentary session has been planned.

- Ludwig Scharinger, chief of Raiffeisenlandesbank Oberoesterreich, says a take over of shares in Bank Austria by Raiffeisen's insurance holding BARC would be a positive move, seeing the costs at eight billion schillings.
- Hypo bank in Salzburg should be privatised by 1997, income from the sale should be used for unemployment programmes, Social Democrats say.
- Provincial electricity providers are against plans by Economics Minister Hannes Farnleitner to create one network and one production company.
- Creditanstalt will be sold to Bank Austria on Friday. Conservatives reluctant to believe it, but coup seems to have succeeded by 99 percent.
